market_name: Will the Iranian regime fall before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the prob move coincides with breaking headlines (strikes, unrest, Hormuz incidents). Confirm crude futures and USO are actually reacting rather than staying flat.
time_plan.1h: Compare Brent/WTI spread and check if energy equities (XLE) confirm the oil bid; verify no denial/de-escalation headlines.
time_plan.2h: Reassess magnitude: is oil trending or fading? Look at options skew and VIX for corroborating risk-off.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate whether the move has persisted into the next session and whether OPEC/US strategic-reserve commentary is capping upside.
time_plan.12h: Mark final return vs 700bps threshold; note if the probability spike reversed (suggesting noise) or held (suggesting real leakage).

predictions.reasoning: A sharp jump in the implied probability that the Iranian regime falls would most plausibly be driven by escalating conflict, mass unrest, or external military action inside Iran. Iran is a major crude producer (~3mbd) and sits on the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of seaborne oil transits. Any credible signal of imminent regime collapse implies supply-disruption risk premium, which flows most directly into crude prices. USO is a liquid, broadly-traded proxy that tracks front-month WTI. In a genuine escalation the move can be violent (700bps+), but on ambiguous probability drift it is more muted, hence a base case around 450bps.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm gold spot and GLD are bid alongside the oil move; distinguish geopolitical bid from rates-driven moves.
time_plan.1h: Check DXY and Treasury yields — a risk-off flight would show gold up with yields down.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether safe-haven bid is broadening (JPY, CHF) or fading.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether gold held gains or mean-reverted as headlines clarified.
time_plan.12h: Record final move; note gold likely stayed sub-threshold, marking this as weak/non-tradable.

predictions.reasoning: A rising probability of Iranian regime collapse signals heightened Middle East geopolitical risk, which typically drives safe-haven demand into gold. GLD is the most liquid gold proxy. However gold moves are usually smaller than oil for a localized supply/conflict shock, and gold is more sensitive to rates/USD than to a single geopolitical headline, so the expected magnitude is modest and unlikely to reach the 700bps tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Market question on Iranian regime collapse by end-2026, topic military_conflict, region middle_east
Iran's role as a major oil producer and controller of the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint
Historical pattern that Middle East escalation drives crude and safe-haven bids
Prediction-market probability shifts as a noisy leading sensor of geopolitical risk
uncertainty_notes: Direction is genuinely ambiguous: a market signal could reflect either escalating conflict (oil up) or an orderly transition/de-escalation narrative (oil potentially down)
A probability drift without a concrete catalyst may not move oil at all — the 700bps threshold requires a real escalation event
Iran's oil exports are already sanctions-constrained, so a supply shock may be partially priced/limited
Gold is confounded by rates and USD, weakening it as a clean proxy

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of Iranian regime collapse most plausibly signals escalating conflict or instability, which transmits to public markets via oil supply-disruption risk (Strait of Hormuz, Iranian production) and a secondary safe-haven bid into gold. Crude (USO) is the most direct and liquid proxy, expected up, though the magnitude only crosses the tradable threshold under a genuine escalation rather than ambiguous probability drift. Gold (GLD) is a weaker, sub-threshold safe-haven confirmation. Confidence is moderate because direction is not unambiguous and the market is a noisy sensor.
key_assumptions: A rising 'regime falls' probability is driven by conflict/instability rather than peaceful reform
Instability raises the oil risk premium via Hormuz/supply fears
USO and GLD are liquid, representative proxies for these risks
The probability move is not already fully public and priced into oil
failure_modes: The oil move reverses if headlines clarify to de-escalation or the probability spike proves to be noise
Regime-collapse expectations could be read bullishly (future normalization of Iranian oil exports), pushing oil down instead of up
The information may already be public and priced, so no incremental asset move occurs
Sanctions already suppress Iranian exports, muting the actual supply shock
Gold's response is confounded by rates/USD and likely stays below the 700bps tradable threshold
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
